conventions.missing: A missing value is JSON null. null never means zero and is never drawn as zero or bridged; the page shows a gap and says why.
conventions.rounding: now.json keeps full precision, because the browser engine recomputes from its inputs; history.json and flows.json store floats to 6 places. The page prints the decimals of the format a value names.
conventions.segments: A sentence is a list of segments. A text segment holds words only. A value segment names its field and holds a value with a format, or an ISO date or a word with its label.

formulas.formula: Q_load = V x fill x K

segments.text: The MMBtu loaded: a carrier of capacity V cubic metres, loaded to the share fill, at K MMBtu a cubic metre.

formulas.formula: G = Q_load x BOR x T_total;  Q_del = Q_load - G

segments.text: The gas used, boiled off or burnt every day of the round trip at the rate BOR, and the cargo delivered; the heel for the way back stays on board. Spark's rate, the hire below, is what a charterer pays less the ballast fuel over the round trip, an owner's earnings rate, so taking it as hire with the heel in G counts the ballast fuel once, never twice.

formulas.formula: C(d, r) = hire x T_total + port(d) + canal(r) + slot premium(r) + ets(d, r) + financing(r)

segments.text: The voyage's cost to destination d by route r: hire for the whole round trip, the ports, the canal both ways, any slot premium, the EU ETS on a voyage into Northwest Europe and the financing of the cargo for the laden days.

formulas.formula: NB(d, r) = (P_des(d) x Q_del(r) - C(d, r)) / Q_load

segments.text: The netback at Sabine Pass per MMBtu loaded, with P_des the delivered price: TTF plus Europe's DES spread, delta_nwe, at Gate, and JKM at Futtsu.
How much more a cargo nets in Northeast Asia by route r than at Gate.

The spread of JKM over TTF at which route r nets what Gate does, in three parts: the gas the longer voyage burns, valued at TTF; Europe's DES spread, which a cargo sold east escapes; and the extra cost of the voyage per MMBtu delivered.

formulas.formula: H*(r) = [JKM x Q_del(r) - (TTF + delta_nwe) x Q_del(NWE) - (C_x(r) - C_x(NWE))] / (T_total(r) - T_total(NWE))

segments.text: The hire at which the two net the same; C_x is the cost without hire. A reported hire below it means the arb was open at the market's own freight.

formulas.formula: lift margin = best netback - m x HH

units_segments.text: A price in euros a megawatt hour becomes dollars an MMBtu at the day's rate in the Federal Reserve's
: USD/MMBtu = EUR/MWh x USD per EUR / MMBtu per MWh. Every price is in dollars an MMBtu, every cost in dollars, every hire in dollars a day.

delivery_segments.text: JKM futures for a month stop trading in the middle of the month before, and Dutch TTF futures two UK business days before the month begins, so from the middle of a month to TTF's last trading day the two front months name different delivery months, and after it they agree again. A week is aligned when every trading day of it names the same month for both, misaligned when none does, and mixed otherwise; the History view rings the misaligned weeks in full and the mixed ones in half. A JKM price is for a cargo delivered in its month to Japan, Korea, China or Taiwan, and a TTF price for gas delivered through its month at the Dutch hub: the two name arrival periods, not loading days. The engine prices a cargo loading in the week at the week's two averages whatever months they name, as a seller choosing a market that week sees them; the voyage east lands three to seven weeks after loading, so a week whose two front months differ sets two arrival periods against each other, and the Model view says of each preset which months its prices name.
